**Chinese name:** 龙芯中科技术股份有限公司 (Lóngxīn Zhōngkē Jìshù Gǔfèn Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Formally established in Beijing's Zhongguancun district in April 2010 with funding traced to China's 10th and 11th Five-Year Plans — the clearest case in this tracker of a design house built explicitly for indigenous instruction-set independence, developing its own LoongArch ISA rather than licensing ARM or x86. Revenue is growing but the company remains unprofitable: H1 2026 revenue reached ¥272 million (+11.6% YoY) with gross margin up 9.6 points to 52.1%, but full-year 2026 guidance of ¥828 million revenue (+30.3% YoY) still projects a ¥230 million net loss.
:::

## What does this firm design?

General-purpose CPUs (the Loongson 3-series and successors) built on the self-developed LoongArch architecture, used primarily in government, state-owned enterprise, and industrial systems, with growing consumer availability. H1 2026 segment mix: informatization/IT chips ¥147M (+27.8% YoY), industrial-control chips ¥68M (-22.6% YoY), and solutions/services ¥58M (+38.7% YoY).
